intro.title: WebSocket Hook
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook that manages a WebSocket connection. You'll learn how to open, maintain, and close a live data stream between your app and a server. The core concept is using React hooks, specifically useState and useEffect, to handle WebSocket events and state. You'll work with TypeScript to define types for messages and connection status, ensuring type safety. By the end, you'll have a reusable hook that can connect to a WebSocket server and display real-time updates.
intro.usecase: WebSocket hooks are essential for building real-time features in modern web applications. You'll find them powering live chat interfaces like Slack or Discord, where messages appear instantly without page refreshes. They're also crucial for financial dashboards that display live stock prices, collaborative editing tools like Google Docs showing simultaneous changes, and multiplayer gaming interfaces that update player positions in real-time. As a developer, implementing WebSocket hooks allows you to create responsive, interactive experiences that keep users engaged with live data streams.
